ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the attached figure, the top branch of the circuit has two resistors, 6Ω and 3Ω, respectively connected between the same pair of left and right nodes, so the top branch is 6Ω and 3Ω in parallel. The middle branch from left to right contains a 1μF capacitor and a 10Ω resistor in series. The bottom branch contains a 10V voltage source, switch S, and a 2Ω resistor; after t=0, switch S closes, and the bottom branch is connected. Reasoning: In DC steady state, the capacitor is equivalent to an open circuit, so the middle capacitor and 10Ω branch do not participate in the steady-state current. The top equivalent resistance is 6Ω || 3Ω = (6×3)/(6+3) = 2Ω. The effective circuit after closing the switch can be regarded as a 10V source driving the bottom 2Ω resistor in series with the top 2Ω equivalent load. By the voltage division relation, the voltage across the top parallel network is 10 × 2/(2+2) = 5V. Since the 6Ω resistor and the 3Ω resistor are in parallel, the voltage across it is equal to the voltage of the top parallel network, so the magnitude of the steady-state voltage across the 6Ω resistor is 5V, rounded to two decimal places as 5.00V.

method.method_draft: First describe the image structure and assign node voltages. Let the left rail be 0 V. Apply KCL at the right rail: current from V to ground through 6Ω plus current through 3Ω plus current through the 2Ω branch to the 10 V source node must sum to zero: V/6 + V/3 + (V - 10)/2 = 0.
